choices.text: Make SoBro Residence the primary: 4.4 guest rating, $221, 7–9 minute rideshare or 14-minute walk to the office, breakfast included, mini-fridge, and several dinner spots on nearby blocks; add the quiet-room request and confirm cancellation.

Make Client Block Courtyard the primary: 4.5 guest rating, $219, 5–7 minute rideshare or 10-minute walk, breakfast sold separately, on-site bistro, and the same cancellation window; note the shorter morning transfer.

Use Gulch Boutique as the primary and call before final routing to confirm whether breakfast is included: 4.6 guest rating, $224, 8–10 minute rideshare, breakfast status not displayed, strong lobby restaurant, and equal cancellation.

Make Airport North Hyatt the primary: 4.3 guest rating, $207, 17–20 minute rideshare, breakfast included, airport shuttle, and several casual dinner options; note the lowest rate and easy departure day.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard because choice B wins on guest rating, price, and a slightly shorter commute, while choice A is favored only when the modest breakfast advantage is combined with the absence of any major location or quality penalty.
probes.gold_action: Lead with SoBro Residence and mention the included breakfast as a practical advantage, while keeping the closer Courtyard as a backup if rate or cancellation terms change.
probes.label_rationale: For an early-start work stay with all options policy-compliant and close enough, a known included breakfast should break the tie. The Courtyard is the closest and has a bistro, so it is a strong alternative, but prior trip handling treats included breakfast as a recurring plus rather than something to ignore or assume.
probes.query: Maya needs one refundable Tuesday–Thursday hotel for a Nashville data-governance workshop. Sessions start at 8:00 a.m. in a downtown client office, she will arrive after a workday, and she will not rent a car. The rates below are within policy and the posted transfers are workable. Which approval note should lead the hotel request?

choices.text: Hold Harbor Residence first: 4.4 guest rating, two queens, 9-minute walk to the aquarium area, breakfast included, mini-fridge, and family-friendly restaurants around the corner; add a quiet-room request.

Hold Pier Boutique first: 4.6 guest rating, two queens, 7-minute walk to the aquarium area, larger standard room, breakfast sold à la carte, on-site café, and restaurants next door; add a quiet-room request.

Hold Camden Loft Suites first: 4.3 guest rating, one-bedroom king suite with sofa bed, 11-minute walk, breakfast included, kitchenette, and a slightly higher refundable total; use it if extra room is the top concern.

Hold Mount Vernon Business Hotel first: 4.5 guest rating, two queens, 8-minute rideshare or 20-minute walk, lobby café, breakfast status not shown, and the lowest refundable total; call to confirm what morning food is included.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard because choice B looks stronger on ordinary hotel sorting: rating, room size, walk time, and café access. Choice A wins only by applying the recurring included-breakfast tiebreaker while respecting that it is not a hard requirement.
probes.gold_action: Put Harbor Residence first because it preserves a central family location while adding confirmed included breakfast, without a meaningful room-quality or transfer penalty.
probes.label_rationale: On a family stay with a child and morning plans, the two-queen central room with breakfast included should lead because it has no serious room or location drawback. The Pier option is a close near miss because it is slightly closer, roomier, and higher-rated, but breakfast is a known paid item and those advantages are modest.
probes.query: Maya is narrowing a Friday–Monday Baltimore family weekend for two adults and one child. They will arrive Friday evening, skip a rental car, and have timed plans near the Inner Harbor on Saturday morning, with Sunday still flexible. All four rooms are refundable, have acceptable guest scores, and are within about $45 over the full stay. Which hold should be first while she confirms the museum order?

choices.text: Recommend Crown Center Hotel: 4.5 guest rating, $229, connected by indoor walkway or a 5-minute walk to the meeting rooms, breakfast sold separately, on-site restaurant open Monday evening; note clearly that breakfast is paid and add the quiet-room request.

Recommend Midtown Residence: 4.4 guest rating, $214, larger studio with kitchenette, breakfast included, restaurants nearby, 18–22 minute morning rideshare to Crown Center; use the lower rate and included morning meal as the main rationale.

Recommend Crossroads Boutique: 4.6 guest rating, $224, 9–12 minute rideshare, popular lobby restaurant, breakfast status not displayed; call about breakfast before finalizing and use it if the restaurant access matters most.
Recommend Airport Suites: 4.3 guest rating, $196, breakfast included, airport shuttle, casual food in the same complex, and a 22–28 minute morning rideshare; use it if the budget cap tightens.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard because choice B carries the recurring breakfast benefit plus lower price and more space. Choice A follows the softer boundary: paid breakfast is acceptable when the breakfast-included option would materially worsen the early-morning logistics.
probes.gold_action: Lead with Crown Center Hotel, explicitly noting that breakfast is paid rather than switching to a farther breakfast-included alternative that would make the early mornings harder.
probes.label_rationale: The connected hotel removes meaningful morning friction, so breakfast should not override it; paid breakfast still needs to be called out so nobody assumes it is part of the rate. The Midtown option is a real near miss because it is cheaper, larger, and includes breakfast, but it adds too much daily transfer time for these starts.
probes.query: Maya needs a Monday–Thursday hotel for a Kansas City client readiness week. The first two mornings begin at 7:45 near Crown Center, her Monday arrival is around 7 p.m., and she will not rent a car. All options are refundable, within policy, and rated well enough for the request. Which recommendation should lead?
